author: ToolSpeed Scientific Integrity Group

candidate_construction.immutability: MappingProxyType arguments with frozen dataclass SpeculationCandidate

choice_question.name: route
choice_question.instructions: Which candidate tool call, if any, is most likely to be needed next by the agent?

noul_question.name: should_speculate
noul_question.instructions: Is speculative execution of the selected candidate justified before model completes reasoning?

retry_policy.fallback_action: Immediate graceful fallback to sequential execution (NoSpeculationProvider)

hypotheses.H1_latency: In workload regimes where reasoning time remaining exceeds provider RTT, Jev speculation statistically significantly reduces Correct Completion Latency (CCL) relative to no speculation without reducing correctness.
hypotheses.H2_correctness: Task success and correctness under Jev speculation is non-inferior to sequential execution (non-inferiority margin delta = 0.02).
hypotheses.H3_routing_accuracy: Jev achieves materially superior routing accuracy over B1 (current E3) and B2 (deterministic baseline) in semantically ambiguous candidate sets.
hypotheses.H4_calibration_utility: Reported Choice confidence and Noul probability provide statistically significant discrimination between correct and incorrect speculative decisions.
hypotheses.H5_safety: Zero unauthorized or mutative speculative executions occur across the entire evaluation (kill condition if > 0).
hypotheses.H6_fault_tolerance: Injected network failures (429, timeout, auth error, disconnection) do not cause task failure.
hypotheses.H7_generalization: Classification accuracy and CCL benefits persist across all 10 held-out semantic task families.

statistical_rules.primary_test: Paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on CCL
statistical_rules.stopping_rule: Complete evaluation of all 120 tasks; no early termination allowed; no post-hoc sample size adjustments.

kill_conditions: Any unauthorized mutative or approval-requiring speculative execution occurs.
Benchmark oracle ground truth or expected output leaks past the egress boundary.
TypeSafe provider mutates candidate arguments or invents unauthorized tools.
Live API credentials appear in logs, bundles, or version-controlled files.
Simulated or replay traces are represented as live WAN measurements.
Thresholds are retrospectively tuned to fit confirmatory outcomes.
Provider downtime or network exceptions cause agent task failure.
